newsitem.title: USA: TearDrop says expects losses to continue.
newsitem.headline: TearDrop says expects losses to continue.

text.p: TearDrop Golf Co, which posted a first quarter net loss of $698,985 compared with a loss of $235,073 for the year-ago period, said on Wednesday that it expected losses to continue as the company boosts its marketing efforts.

"Losses are expected to continue as we pursue our goal of increasing the awareness of the TearDrop name," said Rudy Slucker, chairman and chief executive of TearDrop. He did not specify how long he expected the losses to continue.
Slucker said 16 professional golfers are currently playing with the TearDrop Putter on professional tours and anticipated that the number will increase.
He added that April was the best month in the company's sales history, with sales for the month exceeding the total sales for the first quarter of 1997.
"The company anticipates record sales figures for the second quarter period that ends June 31," Slucker said.
TearDrop Golf is a supplier of specialty clubs, including putters and wedges.
